subject: maths
title: Surface area of pyramids and cones

scenes.heading: Surface area of pyramids and cones
scenes.sub: How much material covers a tent or a party hat?
scenes.say: Tents, spires, party hats and waffle cones are pyramids and cones. Let’s find how much material covers them: their surface area.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Snip a party hat open and it lies flat as a fan shape
scenes.science: A cone’s curved surface unfolds into a sector of radius l
scenes.breaks: A real hat has an overlapping glue tab and no base.
scenes.say: Snip a party hat along its seam and flatten it. You get a fan shape, a slice of a big circle. The hat’s slanted side becomes the radius of that slice, and its area is the hat’s surface area.

scenes.heading: A pyramid unfolds into its net
scenes.say: Here is the net of a square pyramid. First the square base, eight by eight. Then four triangles, each with a slant height of ten. Each triangle is a half times eight times ten, which is forty. So the surface area is sixty-four plus one hundred and sixty, which is two hundred and twenty-four square centimetres.
scenes.caption: The net of a square pyramid: an 8 by 8 base and four triangles with slant height 10. Each triangle is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40. SA = 64 + 160 = 224 cm².

scenes.heading: Two different heights

right.title: Slant height
points: Up the middle of a face

scenes.say: Don’t mix up the two heights. The perpendicular height goes straight up from the centre of the base. The slant height goes up the middle of a sloping face, and that is the one you need for surface area. Find it with Pythagoras.

scenes.heading: Surface area of a cone
scenes.say: For a cone, the surface area is pi r squared for the base, plus pi r l for the curved surface, where l is the slant height. Leave out the base if the cone is open.

scenes.heading: Find l first
scenes.say: This cone has a radius of five and a height of twelve. First the slant height: five squared plus twelve squared is one hundred and sixty-nine, so l is thirteen. The base is twenty-five pi and the curved surface is sixty-five pi. Total: ninety pi, about two hundred and eighty-two point seven square centimetres.
scenes.caption: r = 5, h = 12. l² = 25 + 144 = 169, so l = 13. Base 25π, curved surface 65π. Total 90π ≈ 282.7 cm².

scenes.say: Recap. A pyramid’s surface area is the base plus the triangles, and the triangles use the slant height. A cone is pi r squared plus pi r l. Use Pythagoras to find slant heights, and leave out the base for open solids. Now try the practice questions!
